metrics.population: Every boundary edge of a drawn at-grade surface band, inside the tile proper, that a solved bridge deck continues: marching out along the edge's own outward normal reaches a deck whose top is at the band's height there, within 1.0 m — at the *top*, because a band at soffit level is passing under a low bridge, not handing over to it. 916 edges on asphalt and 339 on ballast; 643 more were skipped because a deck already covers the band's edge in plan, which is an overlap rather than a handoff (`order.deck_above_carriageway`). One abutment contributes several edges, so the population is weighted by how wide the joint is. 184 of 185 drawn decks name the band they continue (`band_class`); the rest fall back to re-deriving the modality from the road class, which is what an archive tiled before that property gives. The band's *interior* mesh is an inset of the paved region and the outer 0.35 m is the separate casing rim, so the march anchors on the interior edge but counts interior and casing alike as surface: what is reported is the distance between the last drawn surface and the first drawn deck. Only surface within 2.5 m of the edge's own height, and of the band's own modality, counts as that band continuing — a region metres below is a road passing under the joint, and a road *approaching* its underpass passes through the height slab too, so without the modality test the march walks the step's reference down the other road's ramp. Counting either shrinks the gap it lies in and hands the step an unrelated height to compare against. Coverage limits, all of them silent otherwise: bores are excluded, since a bore's drawn top is its roof rather than a road surface — a portal needs its own instrument; fitted decks are excluded, since their ends are deliberately walked to seat them (`contact.deck_seat`); a joint that steps by more than a deck thickness plus the slack no longer reads as a handoff and drops out of the population rather than being counted as a huge one; and a deck whose approach band is missing altogether has no edge to anchor on and contributes nothing.

metrics.population: Structure (level != 0) surface samples at the finest measured zoom, against the same class and level in the parent tile one rung coarser — and only where the parent holds exactly one candidate. Structures carry no identity across zooms, so an ambiguous parent would compare two different bridges; those are skipped and counted in the detail line.
metrics.title: Structure height drift between adjacent zooms

metrics.population: Every solved node of every corridor, compared across two solves of one scene. Bit equality: a height that is a function of the model and nothing else cannot move.
metrics.title: The same scene solved twice

metrics.population: Every solved node of every corridor in stratum R or senior to it, compared against the same node in a run where every junior corridor was removed from the scene. Bit equality — a senior height is a function of its own stratum and its seniors, and of nothing else.
metrics.title: Stratum R re-solved with its juniors deleted

metrics.population: not measured
metrics.skipped: no junior stratum in this extract
metrics.title: authority.inversion_S

metrics.population: Every node of every solved profile that the *reconciled* partition leaves at grade, in every stratum, water excluded. Scored by how far the solved road stands from the conditioned terrain reference — in either direction, since a road buried under its own hillside is the same defect upside down — less the class deviation budget, so 0.0 means within the cut and fill the class is built on. Structure nodes are outside the population by definition. Known legitimate tail: a clearance lift raises an at-grade road over a crossing by up to 15 m and keeps it at grade, so a demand-sized excess near a crossing is the model working.
metrics.title: Solved at-grade road standing off its own ground

metrics.population: Every ground layer at every point of a 4 m lattice over the extract: `groundₙ₊₁` against `groundₙ`, and where they differ, whether layer n declares it. Of 10409256 probes, 606480 found a layer moving the ground inside its own footprint — the population the predicate is actually about. Coverage: sampled every 5 lattice steps to stay inside the sample cap; a denser walk would find more.
metrics.title: Ground moved outside the imprinting stratum's footprint

metrics.population: Every place a mapped tunnel span is crossed in plan by another alignment whose own annotation is at grade there — the exact set the solver holds under the ground (the same gate, solve::crossings::covered_sites), and the exact set the crossing machinery waives clearance for. Scored by roof + cover minus this corridor's own terrain, signed: negative is burial margin.
metrics.title: A crossed mapped bore standing clear of its own ground

metrics.population: Every non-grade span of every corridor, scored by the metres of it no derived run of the same kind covers. Metres of centerline, not a count: one long viaduct and a hundred slivers are not the same finding.
metrics.title: Annotated structure the solve does not imply

metrics.population: Every derived run, scored by the metres of it no annotated span of the same kind covers.
metrics.title: Structure the solve implies that nothing annotated

metrics.population: Every annotated non-grade span that a derived run of its kind overlaps, each end scored against the nearest such run's matching edge; the worse end is the sample. Per-end, because pairing whole runs echoed a long span's own length back as "movement" wherever its coverage was fragmented.
metrics.title: How far a structure's ends move when derived
